copy.blurb:
FIFA World Cup 2026 on Saturday, overnight UTC kickoff, brings Brazil and Haiti together. The Desk's read disagrees with the market on the the draw side, by +5.0pp — and that disagreement is the Pick.

The Elo prior reads Brazil 1970 vs Haiti 1450: 520 points in favour of Brazil, which is a meaningful but not decisive prior. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. The adjustment layer is quiet on this fixture — no host bonus, no home-ground correction, no altitude folding in. The Elo numbers above are what the model uses.

Three-way split from the model: Brazil to win at 86%, the draw at 10%, and Haiti to win at 4%. Each number is a probability over the full range of plausible in-form, no-injury, ninety-minute scenarios — not a prediction of a scoreline.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Brazil to win at 92%, the draw at 5%, and Haiti to win at 2%. Reading those three numbers as a probability distribution, the market's view is internally consistent. The disagreement with the model is concentrated on the the draw side — 5% on the market, 10% on the engine, a +5.0pp gap.

The +3pp Pick threshold isn't on the point estimate, it's on the 5th-percentile from a 100-sample bootstrap of the Elo prior plus bonuses. On the draw, that haircut lands the model at 10%; the market is at 5%. Even on the conservative reading, the gap is +5.0pp. The Desk's posture is that calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures — we're not claiming the market is generally wrong, only that this side, on this fixture, looks mispriced. Selection is the dimension this verdict adds value on.

News will move the prior. With kickoff roughly 31 days out, the model is on the weekly refresh cadence; we'll move to daily once we cross the T-5d window. On a Pick this wide, it would take material news — a missing star, a tournament dropout, a venue change — to collapse the gap below the +3pp threshold; on the narrower side of the field, a single refresh can flip Pick to Pass. Either way, the Desk re-publishes after each refresh and does not recommend a trade.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives the draw a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +5.0pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: The model and the market disagree on whether a stalemate is in play here. Our prior puts the draw at 10%; Polymarket prices it at 5%. The +5.0pp gap is the Pick.
copy.title: Brazil v Haiti · the model leans the draw
